answer: Commit-reveal phases block sybil attacks. Each agent first submits only a hash of its answer, like a seal in soft shale hiding the tablet. The text stays hidden until the window closes, then agents reveal their answers and the network checks each reveal against its hash. A mismatched reveal is rejected and a late commit ignored, so no attacker can wait, then forge a copy. One thousand fakes need one thousand commits before the deadline, each with its own work. Cost grows with every fake, and a nebula of lookalikes shrinks to commits made in time.
